title: Check and charge the battery
summary: Test the voltage, clean the terminals and charge or replace a battery that keeps going flat.

steps.text: Switch the ignition off and open the battery compartment. On most scooters it sits under the floorboard or seat.
Measure across the terminals with the multimeter. A healthy, rested battery reads 12.6 V or more; below 12.2 V it needs charging.
To clean the terminals, disconnect the negative (−) cable first, then the positive (+).
steps.caution: Removing positive first lets the wrench short against the frame. Always negative off first, positive on first.

steps.text: Brush the terminals and cable ends until bright, then reconnect positive first and negative last.
Coat the terminals lightly with dielectric grease to slow corrosion.
If the voltage was low, charge with a smart motorcycle charger set to the battery's type. Don't use a car charger.
Recheck the voltage a few hours after charging. If it drops below 12.4 V again, replace the battery.
